title: The Passive-Aggression Strategy: Dominate While Seeming to Submit
coreMove: Under real asymmetry, comply outwardly while quietly building options until direct challenge becomes survivable.
sourcePressure: A weaker operator can be crushed by open resistance too early; hidden construction can be prudent or corrosive depending on whether open disagreement was available.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Use indirect undermining where honest dissent or exit was possible.

hook: Do not open with a battlefield metaphor for The Passive-Aggression Strategy: Dominate While Seeming to Submit.
Do not start by saying strategy is not about violence.
counterintuition: Avoid the reusable correction frame that the move is not X but Y.
Avoid a bland paradox about strength looking like weakness.
tryThisNow: No generic timer, pause, breathe, or list-three-options prompt.
No reusable ask what matters most prompt.
examples: No generic founder in a pitch deck unless the domain requires it.
No battlefield reenactment or invented historical anecdote.
